title: Logging out does not revoke the session: a copied cookie keeps working
what_happens: POST /api/auth/logout only clears the browser's cookie (src/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts). It never calls revokeSessions (src/lib/auth.ts), which is the only thing that bumps users.token_version and makes an old JWT fail stillValid(). A JWT copied before logout (XSS, a shared/public machine, a proxy or access log, a leaked support screenshot, a browser-history-synced cookie jar) is still accepted by the server after the legitimate user has signed out. Verified live against the pass-4 server on port 3176: logged in as citizenA, confirmed GET /api/auth/me -> 200, called POST /api/auth/logout -> 200, then replayed the exact same (now logically 'logged out') cookie value against GET /api/auth/me and still got 200 with the full user object. Citizen tokens last 7 days and staff tokens 12h (src/lib/session-cookies.ts SESSION_MAX_AGE / lib/security/session.ts), so a captured citizen cookie stays live for up to 7 days after the user believes they have logged out, regardless of how many times they press 'Log out'.
what_should_happen: POST /api/auth/logout should call revokeSessions(session.userId) (as reset-password, profile/change-password and auth/security already do) for the portal being signed out of, so a token captured before logout stops being accepted immediately, not after the token's natural 7-day/12-hour expiry. (Logout still only clears this tab's own cookie per existing design; revoking the session is the separate step that is missing.) If logging out is meant to revoke only this one session rather than all of the account's sessions, that needs a per-session identifier in the token (today revokeSessions() uses a single account-wide token_version, so the current primitive revokes every session on every portal, not just the one the user logged out of -- which the fixer should take into account).
repro: node tests/qa/pass4/server.mjs start --port 3176 --frozen --ticking --instance redsec1; then npx vitest run --config vitest.qa4.config.ts tests/qa/pass4/hunt-redsec1.test.ts (the one test is a live repro against that server: login as citizenA, GET /api/auth/me => 200, POST /api/auth/logout => 200, replay the same cookie at GET /api/auth/me and expect 401; it currently gets 200).
evidence: tests/qa/pass4/hunt-redsec1.test.ts (hunt-redsec1-1, it.fails, passes as a confirmed-still-open bug); live run transcript: login 200, me-before-logout 200, logout 200, me-after-logout-with-old-cookie 200 with body {"user":{"id":1000000005,"email":"qa.citizen.a@example.test","role":"citizen",...}}; server log data/aws-cache/qa/run/srv-3176.log shows no crash, i.e. this is the server's deliberate behaviour, not an error path
root_cause_guess: src/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts:1-14 (never calls revokeSessions); contrast src/app/api/profile/change-password/route.ts:39, src/app/api/auth/security/route.ts:47 and src/app/api/auth/forgot-password/reset-password/route.ts:37, which do
class: broken session/auth lifecycle (missing revocation on logout)
skeptic_why: Reproduced on fresh server 3192 (tests/qa/pass4/skeptic-redsec1.test.ts): old cookie still gets 200 at /api/auth/me after logout; no server errors in log. Code agrees: logout/route.ts never calls revokeSessions, and lib/auth.ts line 72 comment says signing out raises the version, so code contradicts its own doc. But the logout route comment says per-tab sign-out is deliberate, the cookie is httpOnly, and an attacker must already hold the cookie, so severity lowered P0 to P1 (broken sign-out promise, not a direct break-in).
